objective: For the cut-open torus at n = 2^m, h = n/2, q = 2n, b in GF(q)*, and X_b the operator F -> (k + 1) F(k + 1) + Omega_b(k) F(k) mod k^h on F[k]_(<h) whose kernel is ker(I + C_s(b^2)) (LINEAR-ROOTS-20261109-001A, Theorem 2): prove (1) the shift and every multiplication are self-adjoint for <F, G> = sum over j < h of [k^j](F G), so X_b is self-adjoint; (2) any two solutions F_1, F_2 have F_1(k) F_2(k + 1) = F_1(k + 1) F_2(k); (3) the solutions are G r(Y), Y = k^2 + k, r in F[Y], deg < h, for one polynomial G = G_b; and, as the target, (4) deg G_b <= h - k_b with k_b = (|K(b) - 1| - 1)/2, which gives the geometric multiplicity |K(b)|/4, and lower bounds on the Jordan chains giving algebraic multiplicity K(b)(K(b) - 2)/8, hence the collapse; or the point where the argument stops. Found by exact computation before registration: (3) with deg G_b = h - k_b for every b at sides 8 to 128.
title: One polynomial per eigenvalue
